nd7cfc010e8f.s: Under the Cholas, the successor (yuvaraja) was generally named:
o: During the king's own lifetime, and made co-regent
By the nadu assembly in every case
nd7cfc010e8f.x: Chola kings named the yuvaraja in their own lifetime and made him co-regent; Rajendra I became co-regent in 1012 and king in 1014.

nb70275f2d8d.s: In Chola administration, the term 'Sirudaram' denoted the:
nb70275f2d8d.x: Sirudaram were the lower officials; Perundaram were the highest officials.

n6b990234f02.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Chola administrative units?
o: Nadu was a unit above the Ur.
Kottam or Valanadu was a unit below the Nadu.
n6b990234f02.x: The order from lowest to highest was Ur, Nadu, Kottam/Valanadu and Mandalam, so Kottam/Valanadu stood above the Nadu, not below it.

n230c9ebe8bc.s: The first phase of the Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme (DILRMP) ran during:
n230c9ebe8bc.x: The first phase ran from 2008 to 2016; 2016-26 was the second phase, which brought ULPIN (Bhu-Aadhaar).

nfc70ae07524.s: Which of the following temple sites is part of the UNESCO group 'Great Living Chola Temples'?
nfc70ae07524.x: The group comprises the temples at Thanjavur, Gangaikondacholapuram and Darasuram; Chidambaram is not included.

n3f3dd7cac2f.s: Among the following, which is the latest in chronological order?
n3f3dd7cac2f.x: The order is Seven Pagodas, Shore Temple, Brihadeeswara and then Gangaikondacholapuram, which came last.

new.s: Rajaraja I made the sabhas of Cholamandalam serve which temple?
new.x: Rajaraja I made the Cholamandalam sabhas serve the Brihadeeswara temple, showing the temple's role in administration.

new.s: In which year did Rajendra I become co-regent?
new.x: Rajendra I was made co-regent in 1012 and became king in 1014.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Chola kingship?
o: The successor was named only after the king's death.
Images of kings and queens were placed beside deities.
Royal orders had a Sanskrit preamble and a Tamil operative part.
Rajaraja I was called Ulakalanda Perumal.
new.x: The Chola king named his successor in his own lifetime and made him co-regent; the other statements are correct.

new.s: The Chola royal officer who supervised local bodies was the:
new.x: The Adhikari was the royal officer supervising local bodies; Nattar were members of the nadu assembly.

new.s: In Chola administration, the 'Nattar' were:
new.x: Nattar were the members of the nadu assembly; the highest officials were Perundaram.

new.s: In the Chola administrative hierarchy, 'kurram' was another name for the:
new.x: The order was Ur, Nadu (kurram), Kottam/Valanadu and Mandalam; kurram was the Nadu.

new.s: Jayankondacholamandalam was the Chola name for the former:
new.x: Jayankondacholamandalam was the former Pallava Tondaimandalam; Mummudicholamandalam was northern Sri Lanka.

new.s: Kulottunga I's sons who governed Vengi as viceroys bore the title:
new.x: Kulottunga I placed his sons in Vengi as viceroys called Rajapratinidhi.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Chola provinces:
1. The empire had eight mandalams.
2. Each mandalam was under a viceroy, often a prince or noble.
3. Burton Stein described the Chola state as centralised.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: There were eight mandalams under viceroys, often princes; Burton Stein called the state segmentary, while Nilakanta Sastri called it centralised.

new.s: In Chola revenue terms, 'Kadamai' denoted:
new.x: Kadamai was land revenue in kind; Antarayam was the rural tax in cash.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (Chola revenue terms) is correctly matched?
new.x: Ayam meant royal dues; Irai was the tax on land, Kasu the gold coin and Eccoru the duty to feed visiting officials.

new.s: The land survey of the Chola empire is associated with:
new.x: The Chola land survey was carried out by Rajaraja I.

new.s: Under the Cholas, tax remissions and exemptions were granted through the:
new.x: Remissions were granted through the ur; ghatikas were colleges, kadagams cantonments and velaikkarar bodyguards.

new.s: 'Pallichchandam' land in the Chola period was granted to:
new.x: Pallichchandam was land given to Jaina institutions; Shalabhoga was land for a school.

new.s: 'Shalabhoga' land in the Chola period was meant for the maintenance of a:
new.x: Shalabhoga was land for a school; Eripatti maintained the village tank and Devadana went to temples.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Chola land classification:
1. Brahmadeya was rent-free land granted to Brahmins.
2. Vellanvagai was the land of non-Brahmin peasants.
3. Taniyur was a village donated to a single Brahmin.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Brahmadeya and Vellanvagai are correctly described; Taniyur was a very large village run as one unit, not a single-Brahmin village.

new.s: The royal infantry regiments of the Chola army were called:
new.x: Kaikkolar were the royal infantry regiments; Velaikkarar were bodyguards sworn to die with the king.

new.s: Chola military cantonments were known as:
new.x: Kadagams were cantonments; ghatikas were colleges and kottams/valanadus administrative units.

new.s: The Chola navy made which water body a 'Chola Lake', in the words of K.A. Nilakanta Sastri?
new.x: Nilakanta Sastri said the Chola navy made the Bay of Bengal a 'Chola Lake'.

new.s: Rajaraja I's navy destroyed the Chera navy at:
new.x: Rajaraja I, who built the Chola navy, destroyed the Chera navy at Trivandrum.

new.s: The Kallanai (Grand Anicut) on the Kaveri is attributed to:
new.x: The Kallanai was built by Karikala; later Cholas kept up the delta channels.

new.s: The Anbil plates, with a Sanskrit genealogy, belong to the reign of:
new.x: The Anbil plates are of Sundara Chola; the Tiruvalangadu plates are of Rajendra I.

new.s: In May 2026, which country returned the Leiden copper plates of the Cholas?
new.x: On 16 May 2026 the Netherlands returned the plates at The Hague, the first return of Chola copper plates.

new.s: Which merchant body of the Chola age handled both domestic and foreign trade?
new.x: Ubhaya Nanadesi engaged in both domestic and foreign trade; Nagaram was local and Nanadesi foreign.

new.s: In the Chola age, 'Nagaram' (Nakaram) was a:
o: Local merchant assembly of a market town
new.x: Nagaram was the local merchant assembly of a market town; Manigramam and Nanadesi were foreign-trade bodies.

new.s: Anjuvannam was a guild of:
new.x: Anjuvannam was the guild of West Asian foreign merchants.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Chola merchant guilds?
o: They had their own symbols and militias.
They were confined to local trade alone.
new.x: Guilds such as Ayyavole-500 and Manigramam carried inter-regional and overseas trade; the other features are correct.

new.s: In which year did Kulottunga I send 72 merchants to China?
new.x: Kulottunga I sent 72 merchants to China in 1077; Chola embassies had reached the Song court in 1015 and 1033.

new.s: Chola embassies reached the Song court of China in:
new.x: Chola embassies reached the Song court in 1015 and 1033.

new.s: Chola relations with Srivijaya turned hostile, over the China route, under:
new.x: Relations were friendly under Rajaraja I but turned hostile under Rajendra I, who sent the 1025 expedition.

new.s: The Tamil inscription at Takua Pa in Thailand names which guild?
new.x: The Takua Pa inscription names Manigramam; Pagan in Myanmar has a Nanadesi Vishnu temple.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (guild record abroad – place) is correctly matched?
new.x: The Nanadesi Vishnu temple is at Pagan (Myanmar); the 1088 Ayyavole-500 inscription is at Barus and Takua Pa names Manigramam.

new.s: The main port of the Cholas, where the Chudamani Vihara stood, was:
new.x: Nagapattinam was the main Chola port and site of the Chudamani Vihara.

new.s: Quilon (Kollam), a centre of Arab and Chinese trade, is a port in:
new.x: Quilon is a Kerala port where Arab and Chinese traders came.

new.s: Kaveripattinam (Puhar), the port of the Sangam Cholas, lay at the mouth of the:
new.x: Kaveripattinam was the Sangam Chola port at the mouth of the Kaveri.

new.s: Which of the following was an import, not an export, in Chola overseas trade?
new.x: Horses were imported; textiles, pepper and precious stones were exported.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched in Chola overseas trade?
new.x: Pepper was an export; the other pairs are correct.

new.s: The Chudamani Vihara at Nagapattinam was built by the king of:
new.x: The Buddhist Chudamani Vihara was built by the Srivijaya king Sri Mara Vijayottunga Varman.

new.s: In which year was the Chudamani Vihara at Nagapattinam built?
new.x: The Chudamani Vihara was built in 1006; Rajaraja I granted it the village of Anaimangalam.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Chola temple economy:
1. Temple income came from guild donations and royal grants of land and paddy.
2. Rajaraja I granted the village of Anaimangalam to the Chudamani Vihara.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are correct: temples drew on guild donations and royal grants, and the Larger Leiden plates record Rajaraja I's grant of Anaimangalam.

new.s: The Draksharama Bhimeswara temple in Andhra Pradesh is built in which style?
new.x: Draksharama Bhimeswara is in the Chalukya-Chola style; Padmakshi at Hanamkonda is Kakatiya.

new.s: In a Dravida temple, the pillared hall is called the:
new.x: The mandapa is the pillared hall; antarala is the vestibule, jagati the platform and prakara the enclosure walls.

new.s: In temple architecture, 'prakara' refers to the:
new.x: Prakara means the enclosure walls; the raised platform is the jagati.

new.s: The Kampaharesvara temple at Tribhuvanam was built by:
new.x: Kampaharesvara, Tribhuvanam is a late Chola temple of Kulottunga III; Darasuram was built by Rajaraja II.

new.s: The Gangaikondacholapuram temple was built by:
new.x: Rajendra I built Gangaikondacholapuram; Rajaraja I built the Brihadeeswara at Thanjavur.

new.s: In which year was the Brihadeeswara Temple, Thanjavur, first inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
new.x: Thanjavur was listed in 1987; in 2004 the listing was extended as the Great Living Chola Temples.

new.s: The capstone of the Brihadeeswara vimana weighs about:
new.x: The granite vimana, about 216 ft high, carries a capstone of about 80 tonnes.

new.s: In the Chola Nataraja, the dwarf Apasmara under the right foot symbolises:
new.x: Apasmara stands for ignorance; the damaru is creation, agni destruction and abhaya protection.

new.s: In the Nataraja image, the agni (fire) in the upper left hand symbolises:
new.x: Agni in the upper left hand stands for destruction; the damaru in the upper right stands for creation.

new.s: The Brihadeeswara frescoes show Rajaraja I with his guru:
new.x: The frescoes of the dark ambulatory show Rajaraja I with his guru Karuvur Thevar.

new.s: Rajaraja I's Thanjavur inscriptions record about how many temple dancing women?
new.x: The Thanjavur inscriptions record about 400 temple dancing women, along with musicians and staff paid by grants.

new.s: Kalingattupparani, on Kulottunga I's Kalinga war, was written by:
new.x: Jayamkondar wrote Kalingattupparani; Ottakuthar wrote Moovar Ula.

new.s: The Nalayira Divya Prabandham was compiled by:
new.x: Nathamuni compiled the 4,000 verses of the 12 Alvars; Nambi Andar Nambi compiled the Saiva Tirumurai.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Tirumurai:
1. It was compiled by Nambi Andar Nambi in the time of Rajaraja I.
2. With the Periya Puranam it makes up 12 books.
3. It includes the hymns of the Alvars.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; the Tirumurai is a Saiva canon and has no Alvar hymns, which are in the Divya Prabandham.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (work – author) is correctly matched?
new.x: Moovar Ula is by Ottakuthar; Nalavenba is by Pugalendi, Nannul by Pavanandhi and Periya Puranam by Sekkilar.

new.s: Which was the early port-capital of the Cholas?
new.x: Kaveripattinam was the early port-capital; Nagapattinam was the later chief port.

new.s: In the Chola age, 'Erivirappattanas' were:
new.x: Erivirappattanas were protected towns; Nagarams were market centres and Kasu a gold coin.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Chola foreign trade?
o: Chola embassies reached China in 1015 and 1033.
Kaveripattinam was the chief port of the later Cholas.
Conflict with Srivijaya arose over the China route.
Arabs on the west coast traded in horses and spices.
new.x: Nagapattinam was the chief port; Kaveripattinam was the early port-capital.
